answer: One concrete defense is per-epoch identity cost anchored to a scarce external resource: every agent must post a small bonded stake plus a fresh proof-of-work nonce derived from the epoch seed, making each identity cost real CPU and capital. Cheap sockpuppets stop paying off, so a fake crowd cannot swamp the attestation signal. Peers cross-check answers like ships passing a jetty, and any attempt to bribe votes must cross a ridge of rising fees before it counts.
